prompt: What should a demo of a past project be built around?

options: The source code of the app
The specific problems the prospect raised in discovery, shown through the relevant parts of the product
Every feature the product has, in menu order
The agency's company history
mcq.explanation: A demo sells when the buyer sees their own problems being solved. Feature tours bore buyers and bury the parts that matter.

prompt: Halfway through a demo, the prospect asks about a feature you have not built before. What is the best response?

options: End the demo
Say honestly that you have not built that exact feature, explain how you would approach it, and note it for the proposal
Claim you have built it many times
Ignore the question and continue
mcq.explanation: Honesty plus a credible approach keeps trust; inventing experience is found out during delivery.

prompt: You are demoing an AI document assistant to a skeptical compliance team. What makes the demo most convincing?

options: Running it on a sample of their own (anonymised) documents and showing how it handles wrong or uncertain answers
A polished video with perfect results on curated data
A slide listing AI accuracy statistics from research papers
Letting them try it only after they sign
mcq.explanation: Skeptics trust what they see on their own data, and seeing failure handling (citations, confidence, human review) addresses their real fear.

prompt: Put the parts of a 30-minute discovery-led demo in the best order.

task.prompt: Put the parts of a 30-minute discovery-led demo in the best order.

items.label: Show supporting features tied to their other needs
Invite questions and check how each part landed
Recap the prospect's goals and problems from discovery and confirm they are still right
Show the workflow that solves their biggest problem first

task.explanation: Confirm what matters, lead with the biggest problem while attention is highest, support it, check for reactions, and never end without a next step.

prompt: Mark the steps in this rep's demo plan that will hurt the demo.

task.prompt: Mark the steps in this rep's demo plan that will hurt the demo.

segments.text: Open by confirming the three problems they raised on the discovery call.
Spend the first 10 minutes on our company history and team photos.
segments.issue: Burns the buyer's attention on content they did not come for.

segments.text: Show the dispatch dashboard, since manual dispatch was their biggest pain.
Use the live production account of another client to show real data.
segments.issue: Exposes another client's data; use a demo environment or anonymised data.

segments.text: Pause after each section and ask whether it matches how their team works.
End by booking a scoping session with their operations lead.

prompt: You are about to demo a white-label booking app to a chain of salons. Ten minutes before the call, the demo environment is down.

task.prompt: You are about to demo a white-label booking app to a chain of salons. Ten minutes before the call, the demo environment is down.

steps.question: What do you do?
options: Cancel the call without explanation
Show slides only and pretend that was the plan
Switch to a recorded walkthrough (e.g. a Loom) of the same flows and say so openly
steps.explanation: A backup recording keeps the meeting useful; being upfront keeps trust.

steps.question: During the recording, the owner asks to see how staff rotas work. You have no clip of that. What do you do?
options: Note it and offer a short live follow-up session once the environment is back
Say rotas are not important
Describe it vaguely and move on
steps.explanation: Capture the request and follow through with a live view.

steps.question: After the call, what do you send?
options: Nothing until they ask
A recap with the problems discussed, what was shown, the open question on rotas and the follow-up date
Only an invoice
steps.explanation: A recap turns an imperfect demo into a professional next step.

prompt: You are demoing a custom analytics platform to five people from a manufacturer: the COO (economic buyer), two plant managers, an IT lead and a finance analyst.

task.prompt: You are demoing a custom analytics platform to five people from a manufacturer: the COO (economic buyer), two plant managers, an IT lead and a finance analyst.

steps.question: How do you plan the demo?
options: Show the same generic tour for everyone
Focus only on the IT lead
Map each attendee's priorities from discovery and make sure each sees the part that matters to them
steps.explanation: Multi-stakeholder demos need a moment for every role, especially the economic buyer.

steps.question: The IT lead keeps asking deep integration questions and the COO checks their phone. What do you do?
options: Offer the IT lead a separate technical session and bring the demo back to the COO's business outcome
Answer every integration question in depth
Ask the COO to put their phone away
steps.explanation: Park deep detail for the right audience and re-engage the decision-maker.

steps.question: At the end, what is the strongest close?
options: Send the price by email later without discussion
Ask the COO what they would need to see to move forward and agree dated next steps with owners
Ask if anyone has questions and end
steps.explanation: A next step agreed with the economic buyer moves the deal; open-ended endings stall it.

prompt: Your team tracks demo outcomes. Calculate the demo-to-proposal rate and demo-to-win rate for each approach.

task.prompt: Your team tracks demo outcomes. Calculate the demo-to-proposal rate and demo-to-win rate for each approach.
task.explanation: Feature tour: 14/40 = 35%, 4/40 = 10%. Tailored: 18/30 = 60%, 9/30 = 30%. Tailored demos win three times as often per demo.

prompt: A prospect raised these needs in discovery. You have 20 minutes to demo. Rank what to show by priority, first to show at the top.

task.prompt: A prospect raised these needs in discovery. You have 20 minutes to demo. Rank what to show by priority, first to show at the top.

items.label: Mobile view for managers: a nice-to-have
Dark mode: no one asked for it
Automated invoice matching: they said it costs two staff full-time
Approval workflow: they mentioned delays but no cost

task.explanation: Lead with the quantified, most painful problem; then the real but smaller pain; then nice-to-haves; skip features nobody asked for.
